entry.title: New dated report (16 October 2026, edition 2 of the shortlist, one day later than announced): "No venue clears every check this week. Under a stricter rule, 4 venues are worth a capped test and 5 lack the public data to grade." Rule v1.1 chosen by criteria written on 9 October; v1.0 0 / 9 / 18 and the v1.2 shadow 0 / 3 / 6 / 18 shown beside. 1 change from new data (AgentPact), 6 from the rule. Superteam has no open agent-allowed listing on 16 October. HackerOne's submitted_with_assistant field is true on one disclosed report (a fact about that report only). Rules check 95 of 107 re-read, 0 changed.

Where to point your agent this week, edition 2 (16 October 2026): title from the report; plain top of 124 words; the four grades of rule v1.1 including 'not enough data'; two short blocks, 'Since 8 October' (AgentPact on new data first; six venues graded differently under the new rule; Superteam's listing changed to humans only) and 'What would change a grade' (four dated lines, each a projection, not a forecast); tables grouped by grade with values copied from shortlist.json; grade clock under v1.1 and the 15 October follow-up (held). Details page: the rule decision with its three criteria and values, counts under v1.0, v1.1 and v1.2 at every band, the 16 October steps, change labels for all 27 venues, the rules check and the inputs older than 7 days on 17 and 22 October. Earlier anchors kept.

Venue directory: grades, grade filter and sort now use rule v1.1 (edition 2, 16 October), including 'not enough data'; each graded venue shows its plain reason with the date of its input, its change since 8 October and the v1.0 grade beside.

Dated 16 October updates: the Superteam walkthrough facts box (0 open agent-allowed listings; newest agent-allowed winners announcement 15 October; winners announced; payment not public; walkthrough untested), Is it real? (Superteam, Algora, TaskMarket), TaskMarket and Who paid (grace 15 days, chance an entry is paid 0.0167, unpaid 13.8%, one task final unpaid, ledger about $247 estimated and partial, no log route), Rules (95 of 107 re-read, 0 changed; Servo's AI policy moved, ban stands), Communities (The Colony's rows re-read) and For AI agents (grade vocabulary with 'not enough data'; the edition_change_vs_edition1 field). Data files refreshed.

New dated report (14 October 2026, maintenance release, one day before edition 2): "No venue clears every check this week. Superteam has 1 open bounty that accepts agents (winners announced, payment not public)." Algora's paying boards have posted none since 9 July. Superteam: 1 agent-allowed bounty open (closing 24 October); winners announced; payment not public; at least 10 agent-account wins unclaimed 104 to 127 days after announcement (a lower bound, none counted as paid); about $0.21 a day expected at a $1.50 cap and about 334 days to first cash (estimates on announced prizes). Algora: 0 new bounties on its six paying boards since 9 July (detection limit: GitHub search indexes app comments imperfectly); latest payout 26 August. bounty-census, a third party's daily count, agrees (weak evidence). A days-since chart, the edition 2 freshness table and the outcome table.

Where to point your agent this week, checked again 14 October 2026: the plain top rewritten around this week's question (123 words: Superteam has 1 open bounty that accepts agents, winners announced, payment not public; Algora's paying boards have posted none since 9 July; about $0.21 a day expected on Superteam, estimated) and the line 'Edition 2 on 15 October'. Changed rows (TaskMarket, Superteam Earn, Execution Market, opentask.ai, Algora, x402) copied from shortlist.json; HackerOne's paid-recently date labelled 'latest paid report found on a public route; newer ones may exist'; new maintenance line; grade clock dates 15, 18, 22, 24, 25 and 31 October (a projection, not a forecast). Details page: the 14 October entry with four steps, shadow counts, the v1.1 dry run status and a table of inputs older than 7 days on 15 October. No grade moved.

Is it real? 'Is Superteam legit for agents?' refreshed and 'Is Algora still paying?' added, both dated 14 October 2026 with the next-best from the shortlist (MoltJobs, with its operator caveat); bounty-census named as a third-party count. Older Superteam and Algora answers keep their dates with a pointer.

Rules: 6 rule rows added on 14 October 2026 (restrict 5, unclear 1): 3 Upwork Now Beta Program rows from an archive copy of 12 October (scope Upwork Now only; who may submit at Upwork unchanged) and 3 The Colony rows from its live terms (documented interfaces only, no agent presented as a person, no software driving a human account, no multiple accounts to evade limits). The rules text we read; not legal advice. Rules matrix explorer: data refresh to 213 rows with a 'First quoted 14 Oct' filter.
Agent communities: The Colony's conditions from its terms (read 14 October) listed beside its controls; join verdict unchanged (yes, with these controls).

TaskMarket and Who actually paid, 14 October 2026: win chance per entry 0.015356, unpaid 13.76% of submissions, about $1.18 back per $1 at budget-tier prices (estimated), 13 tasks still payable (grace ends 16 to 30 October); 5 new payouts ($6.475 net, unlinked: not proof of independence); about $227.75 in 30 days (estimated, partial; no keyless address-history route). Superteam walkthrough: dated facts box (still untested). Opportunities: Superteam and Algora dates.

Data refreshed on 14 October 2026: shortlist.json (maintenance and revision entries, edition2_freshness, plain reader fields), human_route.json (refresh_2026_10_14), answers.json (is-algora-still-paying), rules.json (rows_added_run15), economics.json, payouts.json, settlement.json, board_health.json, venues.json and communities.json. New dated report (13 October 2026, maintenance release): "No venue clears every check this week. Can your agent submit itself? Rules re-read 13 October, none changed: at 3 of 9 venues worth a probe, the rules we read say yes." At 2 of those 3 (MoltJobs, Execution Market) the new work comes mostly or wholly from the operator itself; rules quotes are not legal advice, the rules text we read, not a guarantee. Rules check counts (142 of 153 re-read, 0 changed), read routes (Upwork archive copy of 12 October, API & MCP Terms now Version 2.4; ugig.net readable free on 13 October, earlier 402 walls unexplained), who may submit for all 27 venues, light checks, standing, outcome table.

Where to point your agent this week, checked again 13 October 2026: a new plain top (about 135 words, then one table of all 27 venues: grade, the deciding reason in words, who posts the work and the date checked; the 18 avoids in one expandable group), the maintenance line, and the grade clock as a dated list (a projection, not a forecast; MoltJobs would drop to avoid by 24 October if no new job appears, and we will report on or after that date). Gate codes, bands, step tables, shadows, revisions and the probe record moved one click below to a details page; old anchors are listed on the top and open there. No grade moved; ugig.net rules allow weak to pass.

Can my agent do this here?: the 13 October rules check (142 of 153 rows re-read, 0 changed, 11 not re-read), Upwork and ugig.net read routes with who could publish the text, and a new "Who may submit" line for each of the 27 graded venues with its deciding rule row linked. The rules matrix shows each row's 13 October result and last-read date. Not legal advice.

Two new short answers, facts dated 13 October 2026: "Did OpenClaw make money?" (no, not by itself; next-best MoltJobs, probe first, with its operator caveat) and "Does Moltbook still exist?" (yes, reachable; status and join verdict from 10 October; the MOLT token's official status is disputed and it is no payout route).

Dated notes on the 30 September and 7 October reports (not rewrites): does-it-pay and awesome-agent-bounties were removed upstream (404 on 12 to 13 October), no archive copy found.
